data.reasoning: The disagreement stems from an API error in the qwen3-235b model when attempting to fully review the PKGBUILD, not from any security concern. The deepseek-v4-flash model successfully reviewed all files including the PKGBUILD and found it to be a standard Rust AUR package with pinned source (v0.2.0 tag), pinned SHA-256 checksum, and routine Cargo operations in build functions. Notably, qwen3-235b's own initial PKGBUILD audit (which succeeded before the API error) confirmed 'All code execution deferred to build phase' with no dangerous top-level code. The package follows normal AUR patterns with no injection attempts, suspicious network activity, or obfuscated commands.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement is purely technical: qwen3-235b encountered an HTTP 400 BadRequestError when attempting to audit the PKGBUILD file during the full review phase, resulting in an inconclusive verdict. This is not a security disagreement but a tool failure. The deepseek-v4-flash model successfully completed the same review and found no issues.
coverage_issues: qwen3-235b failed to complete PKGBUILD review due to API error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError)
learnings: API errors during file review should be handled with automatic retry logic rather than marking the entire package as inconclusive

When an initial PKGBUILD audit succeeds but full review fails, the system should distinguish between 'incomplete coverage' and 'security concern' - the former should trigger a retry, not an inconclusive verdict
Models should be more resilient to transient API failures, possibly by caching successful partial results
